title: I left myself a voicemail from tomorrow 📞
style_prompt: dark blue cinematic night, faceless silhouette, fog, minimal interior, no text, no watermark
hook_text: At 4:18 in the morning my phone rang and the caller ID said my own number.

scenes.narration: At 4:18 in the morning my phone rang and the caller ID said my own number.
I answered. For a long second there was only the sound of someone breathing. Then a voice that I knew better than any other said, do not go to work today.
It was my voice. Tired, hoarse, a little bit frightened. It said, I am calling from tomorrow. Tomorrow is not what you think it is.
I hung up. The phone rang again at once. My number again. I let it go to voicemail. A new message appeared, thirty seconds long.
I played it. My own voice, whispering fast, listing things. The lift, the grey coat, the third floor, do not open the door that is already open.
I did what any sane person would do. I deleted it. The voicemail deleted itself, and a message appeared in my inbox that I had never sent.
It said, you have already gone to work. I am the one that stayed behind. The call came from the flat, and the flat was empty.
My phone rang a third time. I looked at the caller ID. Not my number now. Just two words. Your Home. And somebody behind me said, answer it, I am tired of waiting.
So tell me. Do you answer the phone, or throw it away?
